items.title: Does a lineage end by vanishing or by being absorbed? Three cells, no new worlds

The maze differs in amount - identity deaths x2.1, real vanishings 44 -> 105 -> 182, median dead area 27 -> 114 cells - not in kind. The smaller sister is the one swallowed (248:183 in the lattice, 187:98 in the maze). Controls all held: end-survival reproducing X126 to four decimals, heredity 0.548/0.421/0.480, the area budget closing on all 18 000 step transitions, full coverage. items.title: The local budget: isolated, absorbed, vanished, and only then who takes the cells
items.note: All five controls held (end-survival to four decimals, heredity 0.548/0.421/0.480, local and global accounts agreeing on all 18 000 step transitions, fates summing to the deaths, and the pre-declared 20-point drop firing at 29.2). Absorption is about half of all endings (55.3 / 47.8 / 48.4 %), isolated deaths are 31.3 / 29.4 / 21.2 %, real vanishings rise 10.5 -> 21.7 -> 27.4 % (55 -> 183 -> 302 events), and the absorber changes family: 87.2 % kin (54.6 % siblings) in the lattice against 37.7-39.2 % kin and 61-62 % strangers in the percolating cells. So the maze destroys more lineages outright and hands the rest's cells to non-relatives. Report x128b-local, section 10gv.

items.title: Is the kin advantage only geometry? Who lives next door at the same distance
items.note: The planned match on contact distance degenerated - 100 % of the 1 224 partnered absorptions are contact events (median delta 0.66-0.72), partly because the neighbourhood is itself defined as contact plus two cells - and the degeneracy carried the finding: at identical geometry, with one neighbour within reach (median neighbourhood 1.0), that neighbour is a sibling in 87.2 % of 290 lattice absorptions and a stranger in 62 % of 531 maze ones, a 49.6-point difference. So the lattice segregates lineages in space and percolation mixes them, and mixing is the mechanism under the X126 trade-off. Controls: partner counts reproducing X128b exactly, kin nearer than strangers in the lattice, heredity and survival, band population. Report x129-geometry, section 10gw.

items.title: Do sisters merge back, and how long does it take?
items.note: Sisters rarely merge back - 18.4 % of 1 142 lattice pairs (CI 16.1-20.8), 8.6 % of 1 106 in the middle cell, 17.4 % of 1 195 in the maze, with 82-91 % censored - but fast when they do: median 80 / 120 / 60 steps. The two headline numbers (18.4 % of pairs, 64 % of absorptions) carry different denominators and neither explains the other away; birth separation decides a merge (8.06 against 9.27 in the lattice, 11.75 against 24.52 in the maze), which makes it the geometric handle for an interventional test. Controls: the sibling-absorption census reproducing X128b exactly (186/31/57) from an independent script, end-survival reproducing X126, heredity. Two script defects found by those controls (pair ordering in the survival readout, a mean interval printed next to a median) and both rules written. Report x130-remerge, section 10gx.

Controls: the pooled value recomputed from per-world numerators and denominators reproduces every published number exactly. The registered marginal-overlap rule was replaced by the paired test, which the design implies; both results are printed. Report x131-worlds, section 10gy.

The whole identity block is now confirmed at the world level, and the rule for the line is a power calculation before any cross-habitat claim. Report x132-power, section 10gz.

items.note: The mixing length is between 12 and 18 cells and the transition is a wall: 10 of 10 seeds merge at 8 and 12 cells (median 0 and 19 steps to absorption), 20 of 20 keep both lineages at 18, 24, 30 and 36, no seed on the other side of its group. The pattern wavelength here is 12 cells (q'=8), so two lineages merge inside one wavelength and survive as two beyond it - the first interventional support for the segregation reading, and it sharpens it: the two seeded discs are NOT kin, so this is the stranger case, and the block's mechanism reduces to a length (who is within one wavelength of whom). Two defects fixed before reading: the component-count readout is meaningless in a world that fragments into 60-73 spots (replaced by the genealogical absorption rule) and the SEP=6 arm is degenerate because two radius-3 discs touch. Report x134-mixing, section 10ha. Next: X135 (maze), X136 (three inflows at 2-cell spacing), X137 (controlled genealogy).

items.title: The annihilation band: radius 3 gaps 3, 6, 7, 9, radius 4.5 gaps 4, 5, 6
items.note: Mutual coalescence holds in EVERY seed from contact out to a surface gap of 8 cells at radius 3 (gaps 1-8 at one-cell spacing: M 5/5, medians 10, 10, 10, 20, 20, 30, 40, 50 logged steps), then a thinning - 3/5 at gap 9, 2/5 at 10 and 11 - so there is no band and no hole. Mechanism: at gaps 1-8 no seeded disc ever gets a daughter and both lineages end in the new body, while at gaps 9-11 some seeds split at steps 100-170 and the daughters carry the lineage; a lone radius-4.5 disc splits at 150-280 steps and a radius-6 disc at 210-460. items.note: The lone radius-3 disc first divides at a median of 180 steps (320, 160, 150, 180, 180); radius 4.5 gives 190 and radius 6 gives 290, so the split clock is nearly radius-independent between 3 and 4.5. THE SIMPLE RACE IS REFUTED: a pair at gaps 1-8 is one body by step 10-50, three to four times sooner than any disc divides alone, so those mergers are not narrow losses. What survives: at gaps 9-11 the merge takes 70-115 steps and the seeds that end A or P have a disc dividing at 100-170, EARLIER than a lone disc - the approach advances the division. Controls: both reused radii reproduce their split times seed by seed (4.5: 280,190,230,150,150; 6: 210,460,290,290,290), every run one component at the start, nothing empty, none fragmented. items.title: A third radius: does the boundary keep moving inward, and does the time stay put?
items.note: SATURATION, and the registered prediction for the boundary failed in the branch the registration provided. Radius 6 coalesces 5/5 at a surface gap of 7 and breaks at 8 - the same place radius 4.5 breaks - so the boundary moves inward once, between 28 and 64 cells of disc area, and then stops; it is not a smooth function of the radius. The timing law held a third time and more sharply than registered: 29, 39 and 49 logged steps at gaps 6, 7 and 8 on all three radii, and at gap 8 all three radii dissolve the pair at 49 steps even though only three of five seeds coalesce at 4.5 and 6. Report x150-radius6, section 10hk. Next: X151 (radius 5.25 at gaps 7 and 8 - threshold or plateau), X149 (shape of the product, frames), X146 (wavelength).

items.title: Is the stop of the boundary a threshold or a plateau? Radius 5.25 at gaps 7 and 8
items.note: PLATEAU CONFIRMED, with two corrections recorded rather than buried. Radius 5.25 (~87 cells) holds 5/5 at gap 7 and breaks at 8, as radius 4.5 and 6 do: the boundary drops one cell between 28 and 64 cells of disc area and is flat from 64 to 113. Correction 1: my registered branch label for the mixed outcome said 'the creep continues' where three radii breaking at one gap means a plateau - the numbers fired that branch, the criterion was used as written, and the reading is fixed in an amendment. Correction 2: 'at gap 8 all radii dissolve at 49 steps' was a median, false per seed - one coalescing seed in three takes 59 at radius 4.5 and above; the law is exact per seed only while coalescence is universal (20 seed-runs at gaps 6 and 7, exactly 29 and 39). Report x151-radius525, section 10hl. Next: X152 (radius 3.75, gaps 8 and 9), X153 (radius 6 at separation 19.5, sub-cell creep), X149 (shape, frames).
